narrative.overview:
Talim Sahl is the interface of a public institution that happens to be beautiful. It carries the visual grammar of official authority — Navy structure, Teal operational markers, Cobalt commands — but is free of the cold anonymity that plagues ERP software. Every surface signals that serious work happens here, and that the institution chose this product because it reflects their standards, not just their budget.

The system is bilingual by architecture, not by afterthought. Inter and Noto Sans Arabic share the same font stack at the same weight and size. RTL overrides are structural; Arabic text does not feel translated.

Design decisions are made by subtraction. The canvas is quiet so the three brand colors carry meaning when they appear.
keyCharacteristics: Three-color hierarchy with strict role separation (Navy = structure, Teal = state, Cobalt = primary action)
Flat elevation vocabulary: depth from hairline borders and surface tinting, not from shadows
Bilingual-first: Inter + Noto Sans Arabic as a unified stack, not a fallback chain
Institutional density: data-rich layouts with 38px controls, 14px body, 1.6 line height
RTL-safe component patterns throughout (inset box-shadow instead of border-left for sidebar accent)

rules.name: The One-Color-One-Job Rule
rules.body: Navy for structure, Teal for state, Cobalt for action. Never use Cobalt for decoration, Teal for headings, or Navy for buttons.

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: Command Cobalt appears once per screen: on the primary CTA. If it appears more than once, one instance is wrong.

rules.name: The One Stack Rule
rules.body: Inter and Noto Sans Arabic are always declared together. Never separate them. Arabic text that falls back to a system Arabic font will render at a different weight.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: No clamp-based fluid type. All sizes are fixed px values. A sidebar label that shrinks on a narrower panel looks broken, not responsive.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, forms, lists, and panels are flat at rest. The Flat shadow confirms the surface without lifting it.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Cards do not translateY on hover. Hover state is a border-color transition to Trust Teal, nothing more.

dos: Use box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 var(--ts-primary) for the sidebar active indicator — never border-left
Pair Inter and Noto Sans Arabic in every font-family declaration, in that order
Reserve Command Cobalt (#2831AD) for primary action buttons only — one per screen
Use Trust Teal for all interactive state signals: focus rings, sidebar active, hover borders
Express hover state as a border-color transition to Trust Teal rather than translateY or shadow increase
Include html[dir=rtl] overrides for any component using directional properties
Test all text against 4.5:1 minimum contrast, including Muted (#525252) on Canvas and Surface Soft
Include prefers-reduced-motion overrides for every transition or animation
donts: Don't build SAP-gray utilitarian grids — every screen carries the three-color hierarchy
Don't introduce Western EdTech brightness — this interface is for registrars, not students
Don't let the UI read as raw Frappe/ERPNext: unstyled blue links, system-font defaults
Don't use generic SaaS patterns: pastel card grids, gradient accent bars, hero metric templates
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored stripe on cards or list rows
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient)
Don't use glassmorphism as a default — backdrop-filter belongs to modals at most
Don't add uppercase tracked eyebrows above every section
Don't add a fourth brand color — use the established semantic indicator pill vocabulary
Don't use translateY card lifts on hover — the hover contract is border-color only
